artworks.title: Andromeda Chained to the Rocks
artworks.description: Rembrandt's first full-length mythological nude isolates the Ethiopian princess alone on the rock — no Perseus yet, only Andromeda's pale body and the chain that waits for the sea-monster. Oil on panel, Mauritshuis, The Hague.

artworks.title: Andromeda Chained to the Rock by the Nereids
artworks.description: Chassériau paints the Nereids binding Andromeda to the cliff: sea-nymphs and the chained princess before the rescue, Cassiopeia's boast made flesh. Oil on canvas, Musée du Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: Andromeda
artworks.description: Poynter's Victorian Andromeda stands chained against the rock with a blue cloth at her ankle — Ovid and Apollodorus restaged as Academic spectacle, the princess as the myth's still centre before Perseus arrives.

artworks.title: Perseus and Andromeda
artworks.description: Titian's poesie freezes Andromeda on the rock as Perseus dives sword-first at the sea-monster — the Ethiopian rescue as Venetian storm of flesh and foam. Oil on canvas, Wallace Collection, London.

artworks.title: Perseus Freeing Andromeda
artworks.description: Rubens shows the moment the chains give way: Andromeda steps from the rock into Perseus' arms while putti and the slain monster fill the shore. Oil on canvas, Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

films.title: Clash of the Titans
films.description: Harryhausen's film keeps Andromeda at the myth's centre: the princess chained for the Kraken, the sacrifice the city demands, and the rescue that makes Perseus' quest matter.

popCulture.title: Andromeda (constellation)
popCulture.description: The chained princess became a northern constellation — and lent her name to the nearest major galaxy — so the Ethiopian royal's ordeal is written across half the autumn sky.
